title: Dhoklan jo Nach
summary: A men's stick dance from the Thar desert of Sindh, performed at weddings and celebrations, with dancers clashing short sticks to a drum rhythm.
howToPlay: Four hands rise from the tent floor, each holding a thick rope-wrapped stick. Four places are lit: the left pair, the middle pair, the right pair, and all four together.
Strike the place a closing ring marks, on the beat, and the sticks cross and clack together.
Keep a steady count: the clash runs along the row.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Each dancer carries a stick, and pairs knock the sticks together to a ringing beat while circling to the rhythm of a dhol drum. The dance is open to men of all ages.
credits: Tradition: dhoklan jo nach of Thar, Sindh; patterns written for this game
